source_read: PMC HTML, PMC2835832 (author manuscript NIHMS165387): abstract, all sections, Tables 1 to 5 with footnotes as text; read in full before the card was opened. No figures. The supplementary Word file was not opened (no downloads), so the violation rates attributed to Supplementary Tables 1 to 3 were checked only against the text. No funding, acknowledgments or conflict statement on the page. Before reading this source I had seen the vanyukov_2012 card's reporting issue, which quotes Japan figures from Tables 2 and 4. No claims in the task (card check only).

key_findings.note: The 17 Part I samples in Table 1 sum to 85,088; field dates run from 2001 to 2005.
Median recomputed from the 17 Table 2 cannabis totals: the 9th value is 9.8% (Belgium).

Wording of the note: 13 and 7 are the people with the violation (the Table 4 n column). The proportions rest on 16 and 8 people who used other illicit drugs (Table 2), as reporting issue 4 says. The two places should match.
See missed item 2: the 'number of illicit drugs' covariate includes prescription drugs.

Addition for the note: these are pooled per-person-year odds of dependence onset among people who had used each drug, not risks among everyone. The country set differs by outcome: nicotine dependence was assessed in 7 countries and drug dependence in 11 (Table 5, notes 5 and 6). The sample type, recall timing and adjustment set are stated correctly.

reporting_issues.note: Table 2: US 18-29 alcohol 96.2% (n 1318), tobacco or alcohol 96.0% (n 1316); Ukraine 18-29 alcohol 99.7% (n 298), tobacco or alcohol 99.4% (n 297).
Belgium 60+ shows '1.0* (1.0-1.0)'; Belgium 30-44 shows '14.7* (0.9-236.7)'. In Table 4, New Zealand's 28.6 is unmarked while Spain's 7.0 is marked.
Recomputed: the Part I samples of Colombia, Mexico, Israel, South Africa and New Zealand plus the Part II samples of the other 12 countries sum to 54,307, against 54,068 printed.
The n column counts people with the violation: US 126 of 1,258 (10.0% unweighted, 11.4% weighted); NZ 164 of 1,433; Japan 13 of 16; Nigeria 7 of 8; Japan 18-29, 2 of 4.
The same sentence also says 'text' for 'test'.

risk_of_bias.note: ROBINS-E is high overall, driven by confounding and the ecological moderator. The response-rate facts check out: below 60% in five countries; non-response 12.3% to 54.1%.

interpretation_gap.note: 'Minor' is defensible because the abstract and Conclusions hedge ('suggest', 'at least partially', 'suggestive evidence'). The flat statement in 4.2 Conclusions that violations 'are not associated with the development of dependence' should not be repeated in claims (Table 5: 1.6, 1.1 to 2.3; several intervals reach 1.0).

missed: Discussion, 6th paragraph, calls the number of early-onset mental disorders 'an important moderator of risk' for dependence. Table 5 enters them only as main-effect predictors, with no interaction terms, so 'moderator' is not supported. Claims should say 'predictor' or 'associated with'.

Definitions differ. Table 5 note 4 counts prescription drugs among the drug classes in the time-varying 'number of illicit drugs used' (cannabis, cocaine, prescription drugs or other drugs). Elsewhere 'other illicit drugs' excludes prescription drugs (Tables 2 to 5 notes). The 6.1, 15.4 and 35.7 odds ratios in key finding 5 therefore include non-medical prescription drug use as a class.

Minor reporting slip: the Table 1 note on sample design speaks of 'Nine of the 15 surveys' being nationally representative, while the paper pools 17 countries. The count matches neither the countries nor Table 1.
